dependency_graph.why: AC-6's directoriesToRefresh() reads file-job:done.affectedDirectories, a field IR-FOP-002 AC-4 defines; without it the hook cannot know which directories to invalidate.
the '..'-exclusion parser feeds the same childrenByPath the hook owns; there is exactly one place raw listDirectory responses become nodes.
click/selection decisions operate on selectVisibleRows() and the selection/expansion reducer state FR-FEX-001 defines.
the '..' row is excluded from decideDoubleClick/click handling entirely, by never appearing in the rows those functions see.
mode and sort live in the same per-tab tree state FR-FEX-001 defines.
list-mode directory double-click reuses decideDoubleClick's mode-aware branch rather than a separate handler.
each tab owns an independent useFileTree instance; tab state is a record of FR-FEX-001's per-instance state.
mode and sort are persisted per tab, per workspace — the thing being persisted is FR-FEX-002's state.
paste/copy/cut menu items are enabled from the same clipboard FR-FEX-005 owns.
'편집기로 열기' is enabled by the same isViewableExtension-backed openable check FR-FEX-011 AC-6 defines.
the list-mode menu variant (AC-8) is keyed on the same mode field FR-FEX-002 defines.
buildPasteJobRequest's output shape is a direct match of IR-FOP-001 AC-1/AC-2's POST /api/file-jobs body — a server-contract dependency across the FEX/FOP scope split.
F2/rename and the mobile button row reuse FR-FEX-006's single-selection and clipboard-non-empty enablement predicates rather than redefining them.
all three entry points call the same decideOpenFileExplorer/getFileExplorerDialogId pair FR-FEX-003 AC-1/AC-2 define.
the '↑' enablement signal (AC-4) is the same hasParent() output CON-FEX-001 AC-6 already defines for parsing purposes.
AC-5's commit/rollback discipline around a rejected navigate-up lives in the same root-navigation state machine FR-FEX-001 owns.

ambiguities.issue: design.md §7 says the list-mode menu 'drops only 새 탭에서 열기' but does not say whether that item is omitted from the array or present-and-disabled. FR-FEX-006 AC-4's own phrasing ('...일 때만 활성') suggests disabled is the general pattern for every other item, which would argue for disabled-not-omitted here too for consistency; but the mockup.html host.dataset.newtab gate (line 1554, 1630) treats it as a boolean that can also be false for reasons unrelated to mode, which reads more like an omission/exclusion signal.
ambiguities.proposed_resolution: Omit the item entirely in list mode (matches the mockup's data-driven exclusion and needs no separate disabled-styling rule); assert absence from the array in the AC-8 test rather than presence-with-disabled:true.

ambiguities.issue: 'no virtual scroll, all rows present in DOM' is fundamentally a rendering guarantee. A source-text guard (no import of a named virtualization library) only rules out the specific libraries checked for — a hand-rolled windowing implementation using plain refs/IntersectionObserver would pass the guard while still violating the AC.
ambiguities.proposed_resolution: Treat the source-text guard as a cheap regression trip-wire only, not the primary evidence. Require the browser_only Playwright row-count/name-lookup test (against https://localhost:2222, per this repo's testing rules) as the actual gate for this AC when the implementing skill closes it out.

ambiguities.issue: AC-7 is in this chunk's scope, but its subject (the editor left panel's tree surface) is FR-MDE-012, explicitly listed as later-plan work. The pure decision function can be written and tested now against a synthetic scope id, but there is no real panel to wire it to yet, so this chunk cannot produce end-to-end verification of AC-7, only the reusable building block.
ambiguities.proposed_resolution: Accept the pure-function test as this chunk's complete discharge of AC-7's testable surface; track the real wiring explicitly as a seam filled by FR-MDE-012 (see seams_for_later_plan) rather than leaving AC-7 silently unaddressed.

ambiguities.issue: Same root cause as FR-FEX-005 AC-7: '새 탭에서 열기는 탐색기 창의 디렉터리일 때만 활성' implies a context distinction (explorer window vs. editor panel) that only becomes meaningful once FR-MDE-012 exists. Building buildFileExplorerContextMenuItems with an info.context parameter now is speculative in the sense that only one context value ('explorer-window') is ever exercised by this chunk's tests.

ambiguities.issue: The requirement says a blocked-parent listing failure must 'show the error to the user' but does not specify the UI surface. FR-FEX-007's window-scoped modal (the natural home for this) is explicitly later-plan; a global toast would work but is not mentioned anywhere in design.md for this specific failure mode, and design.md's decision-modal discussion (§5) is scoped to copy/move/delete flows, not navigation.
ambiguities.proposed_resolution: Use a lightweight inline error state surfaced near the path bar / '↑' button (non-modal, e.g. a transient message or error icon with tooltip) for this chunk, and re-route it through FR-FEX-007's window-scoped modal once that lands if a stronger interrupt turns out to be needed — same shape as the other FR-FEX-007 seams in this document.

ambiguities.issue: The AC says all three entry points must raise rather than close an already-open window, but the header icon button (AC-5) and terminal menu (AC-4) are new call sites with no existing analogue in this repo to check for a competing 'close on second click' convention the way MetadataRow's cwd-menu already has one for other actions. It is not fully certain from the design doc whether the header button should be a toggle (open/close) rather than an always-open-or-raise action.
ambiguities.proposed_resolution: Read design.md §9.2 and §12 as decisive: they describe only '열기' entry points and 'raise, never close' for all three, with no toggle behavior mentioned anywhere. Implement the header button as always open-or-raise, never a close-toggle, consistent with the other two entry points and with decideOpenFileExplorer's two-branch (raise|create) contract, which has no 'close' branch at all.
